abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) could transform evidence synthesis and revolutionize the global scientific enterprise, yet its agricultural applications are understudied.Here, we systematically assess the performance of three web-grounded AI engines (ChatGPT, ScholarAI and DeepSeek) in synthesizing the global literature on biological control of the fall armyworm Spodoptera frugiperda, and benchmark their outputs against a recent, near-exhaustive human review.Though all engines rapidly screened vast literature corpora, they exhibited shortcomings in factual accuracy, reporting reliability and data consistency.In machine-run syntheses, natural enemy prevalence and performance data often diverged from published records while the level of agreement in enumerating top-performing taxa was evenly low.Meanwhile, internal consistency between laboratory and fieldlevel parasitism data for ScholarAI and DeepSeek was similar to that in human-run reviews.All models tended towards faulty data extrapolation, hallucination and data fabrication, and a sporadic exclusion of key species.While autonomous, machine-only efforts accurately capture coarse-grained patterns in natural enemy identity, abundance, and impacts, they carry limited utility for (living) evidence syntheses or rigorous decision-support.Yet, handled with prudence and due human oversight, machine power might eventually revitalize underfunded disciplines and advance nature-friendly farming.

title: Computer vision based automated quantification of agricultural sprayers boom displacement
abstract: Application rate errors when using self-propelled agricultural sprayers for agricultural production remain a concern. Among other factors, spray boom instability is one of the major contributors to application errors. Spray booms' width of 38m, combined with 30 kph driving speeds, varying terrain, and machine dynamics when maneuvering complex field boundaries, make controls of these booms very complex. However, there is no quantitative knowledge on the extent of boom movement to systematically develop a solution that might include boom designs and responsive boom control systems. Therefore, this study was conducted to develop an automated computer vision system to quantify the boom movement of various agricultural sprayers. A computer vision system was developed to track a target on the edge of the sprayer boom in real time. YOLO V7, V8, and V11 neural network models were trained to track the boom's movements in field operations to quantify effective displacement in the vertical and transverse directions. An inclinometer sensor was mounted on the boom to capture boom angles and validate the neural network model output. The results showed that the model could detect the target with more than 90 percent accuracy, and distance estimates of the target on the boom were within 0.026 m of the inclinometer sensor data. This system can quantify the boom movement on the current sprayer and potentially on any other sprayer with minor modifications. The data can be used to make design improvements to make sprayer booms more stable and achieve greater application accuracy.

title: Fusion of multimodal features acquired by custom-developed computer vision and electronic nose equipment for the detection of Huanglongbing at various symptomatic stages
abstract: Citrus is widely loved for its rich nutritional value and unique flavor, and also occupies an important place in agriculture and the economy. The citrus industry has suffered severe losses in recent years due to the proliferation of citrus Huanglongbing (HLB). The transmission of HLB occurs via the Asian citrus psyllid insect vector and grafting practices, with no efficacious therapeutic intervention identified to date, aside from mitigating its dissemination through prompt identification and eradication of infected citrus trees. Detection of HLB is difficult due to its incubation period and the variety of symptoms at different stages of infection. Hence, there exists a pressing requirement for a detection methodology capable of integrating multi-level features of HLB to facilitate precise identification of the disease across various stages of infection. Most of the existing assays use single sensing, which leads to limitations and incompleteness in identifying specific markers induced by HLB. In this study, the effective configuration and complementarity of multimodal sensory information is achieved by establishing a fusion and complementary mechanism at the level of pre-processing and analyzing multisource information. The extraction of computer vision and electronic nose features of citrus leaves was realized using custom-developed portable detection devices. The performance of HLB detection was compared on different datasets obtained by multimodal feature fusion methods which include direct fusion method, stepwise fusion method and the improved Recursive Feature Elimination and Cross Validation (RFECV) feature selection method. The improved RFECV feature selection method uses the RFECV algorithm for each classification step in the delineated stepwise classification model and performs the feature set preference by cross-validation. The final improved RFECV feature selection method worked best for fusion of visual and olfactory features with an accuracy of 95.38% for HLB samples at various symptomatic stages, with 94.23% for early stage HLB and 94.12% for Zn Def. & HLB-positive samples. Multimodal feature fusion for feature acquisition proved to be superior to feature acquisition from a single sensing source, with enhanced fusion of HLB-induced feature sets at the visual and olfactory levels. It helps to improve the stability of the HLB measurement model to achieve the detection of HLB samples in complex environments. This method can provide generalized technical support for the application of multi-source sensing information and multimodal feature fusion methods in plant disease detection.

title: Optimising automatic cattle weight estimation based on computer vision through animal temperament assessment
abstract: Conventional cattle weighing approaches are labour-intensive, time-consuming, and can cause stress, which negatively affects animal health and production. Automated, contactless methods using computer vision and machine learning technologies have been proposed to address these issues. These methods enable the accurate estimation of animal weight by analysing RGB-D images from a depth camera, thereby eliminating the need for manual weighing and reducing stress in animals. Temperament assessments in beef cattle, particularly exit velocity and flight speed, provide critical insights into growth performance, feed efficiency, and carcass quality. The potential of incorporating speed features into morphometric data can lead to a stable improvement in the quality of the live cattle weight prediction model. This study aimed to develop an algorithm for estimating cattle movement speed using the YOLOv8n neural network on RGB-D images, integrate these speed features with traditional morphometric data, and evaluate the resulting improvements in predicting live cattle weight. This study showed that for the ExtraTrees model, R 2 increased by 0.04 on the test, while MAE decreased by 1.9 kg. The proposed model is a promising approach for practical application due to the combination of high performance and automation.

title: Automated detection and localization of hoof diseases in dairy cattle using an integrated computer vision and infrared thermography system
abstract: Hoof diseases are a major cause of lameness in dairy cattle, resulting in significant welfare concerns and economic losses. Early detection remains challenging due to the limitations of visual inspection and manual scoring, particularly in large herds. This study presents an integrated infrared thermography (IRT) and deep learning system for automated detection and localization of hoof diseases under real farm conditions. Unlike previous IRT approaches that relied on manual thermal data analysis, our system combines automated hoof detection, classification of hoof health, and intra-hoof temperature mapping to identify pathological changes at scale. A dataset of 14,322 infrared images with 48,427 annotations was collected from 160 Holstein cows on a commercial dairy farm. The system demonstrated superior hoof detection accuracy using YOLOv8-large (mAP@50 ≈ 0.97) and reliable health classification, with MobileNetv3 providing an effective balance between accuracy and real-time inference speed. The approach enables early, non-invasive monitoring of hoof health, supporting practical deployment in precision livestock farming. At the same time, challenges such as dataset imbalance and the need for broader validation across farms remain, outlining clear directions for future research.

title: A novel approach to monitor peanut equivalent water thickness through modular training and transfer learning of an improved PROSAIL model using a Wasserstein generative adversarial network
abstract: Empirical and physical models are widely used for monitoring equivalent water thickness (EWT) to adjust plant moisture management. However, model transferability to different times and locations, and insufficient training data remain the two key challenges of field spectroscopy analysis. Therefore, this study aims to construct a hybrid model, which combines the physical models optimized by Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Nets (WGAN) and empirical models for performing hyperparameter searches (the process of finding optimal model settings) to monitor the peanut EWT. Specifically, we develop a large spectral dataset consisting of field-measured data which including 246 peanut varieties in five peanut farms across China and synthetic datasets generated from the physical models optimized by WGAN. Furthermore, the PWLEH was constructed by hyperparameter tuning and pre-training which using synthetic datasets, and then fine-tuned by modular training with field data of peanut canopy water content. Comparing the model constructed with field data (R2 = 0.5618, mean squared error (MSE) = 0.0725) and PROSAIL (a widely used canopy radiative transfer model) (R2 = 0.7105, MSE = 0.0473), PWLEH achieved high accuracy in predicting peanut water content (R2 = 0.7650, MSE = 0.0519). Unlike pure data-driven approaches, the new hybrid model incorporated radiative transfer knowledge and obtained higher predictive performance with fewer field data. This study demonstrates the potential of applying an optimized PROSAIL, hyperparameter search and modular training to improve the accuracy and transferability of the EWT prediction model, providing a new approach for sustainable agricultural management.

title: Generative data augmentation for AIoT-based smart pig farming: The PigTalk 2.0 system
abstract: Piglet mortality is a significant issue on pig farms. Often, piglets do not receive proper care after birth or are crushed by the sow, leading to the death of 2 to 4 piglets during each farrowing process. This represents a substantial loss for pig farmers. To address these issues, this paper presents the development of the PigTalk2.0 system, which is based on the Artificial Internet of Things (AIoT) and image recognition technology, aimed at preventing piglet deaths caused by crushing by the sow. Since collecting large-scale agricultural datasets is costly and labor-intensive, Since collecting large-scale agricultural datasets is costly, this study proposes a hybrid augmentation strategy. We combine conventional techniques (e.g., translation, flipping) with Generative AI-based data augmentation to effectively expand limited datasets and enhance model robustness, providing synthetic diversity that strengthens model training. PigTalk2.0 uses image recognition to monitor the posture of the sow. To prevent the sow from accidentally crushing the piglets when she suddenly lies down, the system activates an air blower to gently push the piglets away when the sow stands up. Additionally, PigTalk2.0 can detect when a sow is about to farrow for the first time, allowing the system to notify the farm administrator to check the piglets’ health and provide necessary care immediately after birth. The results demonstrate that introducing consumer IoT technology into family-run agriculture or medium- to large-scale enterprise-run pig farms can significantly improve productivity.

title: AMGAN: A multimodal generative adversarial network for near-daily alfalfa multispectral image reconstruction
abstract: Accurate and temporally consistent multispectral observations are essential for monitoring alfalfa yield and quality, given its frequent harvest cycles and rapid regrowth. However, optical satellite imagery is often constrained by cloud cover, revisit intervals, and sensor availability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel Alfalfa Multimodal Generative Adversarial Network (AMGAN) designed for near-daily multispectral image reconstruction. Unlike conventional image-to-image or spatiotemporal fusion methods that overlook crop-specific characteristics, are restricted to observed timestamps, or depend heavily on dense temporal series, AMGAN leverages multisource (Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-1, PlanetScope) and multimodal (climate, geographic, temporal) information within an adversarial learning paradigm. This enables high-quality image generation from minimal inputs. Extensive experiments across five major alfalfa-producing states in the United States (2022–2024) show that AMGAN consistently surpasses four state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning baselines. It achieves higher reconstruction accuracy across all spectral bands, with pronounced gains in red-edge and near-infrared (NIR) regions critical for vegetation assessment. Multisource integration and multimodal cues enhance robustness, ensuring reliable performance under diverse observation scenarios. The reconstructed imagery was subsequently evaluated in alfalfa yield and quality prediction tasks. Results demonstrated high predictive accuracy for dry matter yield (DM) in the cross validation (CV) experiment with a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.80, and moderate correlations for selected quality traits such as crude protein (CP), non-fiber carbohydrates (NFC), and minerals, while nutritive value traits tied to complex biochemical processes remained more challenging. Overall, this study underscores the potential of multimodal adversarial learning to bridge observational gaps in alfalfa monitoring. The proposed framework provides a scalable, crop-specific approach for generating temporally dense imagery, supporting precision management for biomass-related and proximate quality traits, while performance for digestibility traits remains limited.

title: Agricultural autonomous decision-making system ”Fuxi Brain” Based on generative large model fusion internet of things
abstract: Precise decision-making in agricultural production has always been a key bottleneck restricting the development of modern agriculture. Traditional decision-making models that rely on manual experience are no longer able to meet the needs of modern intelligent agriculture. This study, by integrating the Agricultural Internet of Things (IoT) with generative big models, has realized a fully autonomous agricultural intelligent system called the ”Fuxi Brain.” This system consists of two parts. The first part constructs a comprehensive ”sky-air-ground-human-machine” data collection system, enabling digital perception of all factors in agricultural production. The second part is the intelligent decision-making system. First, within the brain’s dynamic decision-making layer, a multi-agent collaborative architecture based on a hybrid multi-model (a general big model + a specialized agricultural model) is proposed. Furthermore, a dynamic optimal matrix algorithm (DOMA) is designed to improve the system’s decision-making efficiency significantly. Finally, a full-modality alignment training method is developed to effectively address the challenge of integrating multi-source heterogeneous data. Experimental results show that, in the AlpacaEva and MT-Bench benchmarks, the system’s decision accuracy improved by 36.7 percentage points compared to mainstream models such as ChatGLM. The full-modal alignment training method significantly outperformed traditional methods in cross-modal understanding tasks. Test results on a one-stop agricultural service decision-making platform demonstrated an accuracy rate of 92.3% compared to those of human experts. In an actual application on a 1367-acre corn planting site at Dahewan Farm in Inner Mongolia, the system autonomously generated 127 decisions throughout the production cycle, achieving an accuracy rate of 89.7%. This successfully enabled autonomous and precise decision-making throughout the entire process, from planting to harvesting. This research provides innovative technical paths and practical examples for the development of intelligent agriculture.

title: Hierarchical control strategy for improving rotary tillage stability and efficiency of hybrid tractors using regenerative braking
abstract: High-quality tractor rotary tillage operations face significant challenges under complex environmental conditions. To overcome this, a front-axle direct torque-coupled hybrid tractor powertrain (FADTC-HTP) is proposed, aiming to improve energy efficiency and path stability via coordinated control of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) regenerative braking and an electronically controlled limited slip differential (eLSD). Based on the proposed powertrain, a hierarchical control strategy is developed, combining dual-stage model predictive control with reinforcement learning. First, a hidden Markov model (HMM)-based dual-stage linear time-varying MPC(HMM-DLTV-MPC) is designed as a supervisory controller to enable high-precision nonlinear dynamics approximation, adaptive parameter updating, and dynamic decoupling. To address the challenge of achieving optimal control of a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) nonlinear tractor system under random disturbances, an enhanced Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)-based subordinate controller is proposed to improve robustness and efficiency. Specifically, the controller incorporates expert experience guidance to inject prior knowledge and introduces a control target self-correcting mechanism to adaptively mitigate control errors caused by environmental uncertainties. Furthermore, by integrating long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with self-attention modules, the controller substantially strengthens the agent’s ability to capture complex multidimensional temporal dependencies, thereby significantly boosting both control performance and training efficiency. Agent training is conducted in a simulation environment constructed from real-world field traction data and soil cone index distributions. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments show that the proposed method improves energy efficiency by up to 11.14% and reduces lateral path deviation by 76.47%. It also significantly reduces dependence on front-wheel steering compensation. These results demonstrate that the proposed powertrain and control strategy can effectively enhance both energy efficiency and operational stability in hybrid tractor applications. This study provides a new perspective on novel hybrid tractor powertrains and intelligent control strategies.

title: Computer vision-based body measurement of cattle and pigs: A systematic review
abstract: As the global population grows, the increasing demand for meat is driving the rapid expansion of the livestock industry, making production efficiency a central priority in modern livestock production systems. Body measurements collected during rearing provide essential phenotypic indicators of growth performance, reproductive potential, genetic background, nutritional status, and overall health. They also serve as key inputs for precision livestock management applications, including body weight estimation, growth modeling, and carcass or meat quality assessment, thereby improving production efficiency. However, conventional manual measurement methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and operator-dependent, creating a major bottleneck for precision livestock farming. Recent advances in machine vision and three-dimensional reconstruction have accelerated the automation of body measurement. However, existing studies remain fragmented and lack a unified technical framework, thereby limiting standardization and large-scale deployment. This review synthesizes recent advances in automated body measurement for cattle and pigs and proposes a unified conceptual and technical framework. First, it formalizes commonly used body traits by providing standardized definitions of key morphometric indicators. From the perspective of data acquisition, measurement data are categorized as two-dimensional (2D) or three-dimensional (3D), and mainstream acquisition schemes ranging from single-view RGB cameras to multi-view depth sensors are compared and further classified as fixed or mobile platforms according to their practical applicability. From an algorithmic perspective, the workflow is organized into two major stages: data preprocessing and feature extraction. The former summarizes classical image-processing methods and deep learning-based segmentation approaches, whereas the latter estimates morphometric features and computes body traits using geometry-based and learning-based methods in both 2D and 3D settings. To support method development, evaluation, and benchmarking, representative public datasets are also reviewed. Finally, this review discusses key technical challenges and future directions, including multimodal fusion, end-to-end intelligent systems, and real-time dynamic monitoring, with the aim of advancing both theoretical research and practical applications in precision livestock management.

title: Short-term time series predictions of greenhouse gas emission from dairy houses based on diverse machine learning models
abstract: Open-type dairy houses are significant sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, yet accurate quantification remains challenging due to complex indoor-outdoor environmental interactions and the prohibitive costs of continuous monitoring. Furthermore, existing predictive research predominantly relies on monolithic models that struggle to balance computational efficiency with the highly diverse volatility profiles of different trace gases. To address these deficiencies, this study proposes a novel, adaptive Hybrid Time Series Prediction (TSP) framework tailored for short-term GHG emission forecasting. The framework's architecture is grounded in a systematic multi-paradigm evaluation encompassing statistical (ARIMA), classical machine learning (SVM), and deep learning (BPNN, LSTM) models. Utilizing continuous monitoring data (CO 2 , N 2 O, NH 3 , and CH 4 ) from 10 sampling points across two naturally ventilated dairy houses, we conducted a comprehensive multi-dimensional assessment encompassing computational efficiency, predictive precision, spatial–temporal robustness, and cumulative error propagation mechanisms to optimize gas-specific model allocation. Results reveal a critical performance divergence contingent on gas characteristics: for high-concentration, stable gases (CO 2 and CH 4 ), the Support Vector Machine (SVM) exhibits an optimal balance of ultra-fast computational speed, minimal memory consumption (1–3 MiB), and robust accuracy. Conversely, for low-concentration, highly volatile trace gases (N 2 O and NH 3 ), the Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN) demonstrates superior non-linear mapping capabilities to filter stochastic noise. By adaptively integrating SVM and BPNN, the framework successfully minimizes asynchronous estimation errors. Additionally, a 5–10 min sampling interval was identified as the optimal operational balance. This hybrid approach offers a cost-effective, highly accurate solution for real-time GHG monitoring, demonstrating significant potential for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in the global precision livestock sector.

title: Automated computer vision monitoring of black soldier fly larval growth using metaheuristic optimization for waste-to-feed bioconversion
abstract: Sustainable conversion of organic byproducts into agricultural resources is vital for achieving circular bioeconomy goals. The black soldier fly (BSF, Hermetia illucens) offers an efficient bioconversion pathway, transforming organic residues into protein-rich feed and biofertilizer. However, variability in feed composition and high labor requirements constrain the scalability and profitability of BSF-based waste-to-feed systems. This study introduces an automated computer vision framework for monitoring the growth of black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) using instance segmentation and metaheuristic optimization. Sewage sludge from Taiwan’s wastewater treatment plants was used as a feed substrate, and a Pilgrimage Walk Optimization (PWO) algorithm was integrated with a You Only Look Once version 11-instance segmentation model (YOLO11-seg) to enhance hyperparameter tuning and detection accuracy. The model achieved high precision in estimating larval surface area and converting it to biomass weight, enabling real-time, non-contact monitoring of growth performance. An economic analysis using Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) demonstrated that a 1:1 sludge-to-wheat bran mixture significantly improved bioconversion efficiency and financial returns, underscoring the feasibility of AI-driven computer vision for intelligent insect farming, organic waste valorization, and sustainable waste management. Nevertheless, these findings are based on laboratory-scale experiments, and field-scale studies are needed to validate scalability and real-world implementation.

title: Deformable transformer framework for automated calf respiratory health scoring
abstract: • Developed a deformable transformer framework for calf respiratory health scoring. • Evaluated model on real-farm images across ocular, nasal, and ear indicators. • Built a dataset of 5,374 annotated frames from 100 Holstein calves. • Verified interpretability through Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions. Respiratory diseases significantly impact calf health, welfare, and productivity. Traditional health evaluations rely on subjective human observation, leading to inconsistent diagnoses and scalability challenges in large herds and group housing systems. This study proposes a computer vision framework that automates visual health scoring of calves using images captured by mobile devices under natural farm conditions. The model focuses on key phenotypic indicators—ocular discharge, nasal discharge, and ear posture—associated with bovine respiratory disease. A vision transformer-based architecture was developed, incorporating a Swin Transformer backbone for multi-scale feature extraction, a deformable attention encoder for spatial adaptability, and a query-based decoder to perform 4-class classification aligned with standard scoring guidelines. A dataset of 5374 annotated frames from 100 Holstein calves was collected and labelled by three trained individuals using a standardized 4-point respiratory health scoring system. Evaluation on field-collected data achieved strong performance on the ocular task (Precision: 0.87, Recall: 0.85, F1-score: 0.86), nasal task (Precision: 0.86, Recall: 0.89, F1-score: 0.88), and ear posture task (Precision: 0.75, Recall: 0.90, F1-score: 0.82). Comparative analysis with baseline architectures confirmed the superiority of our method particularly in handling subtle variations in mild and moderate symptoms. Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that the model attends to biologically relevant regions. Additionally, an annotation consistency analysis was conducted and found that inter-annotator agreement significantly influenced model performance, especially in ambiguous scoring cases. These findings highlight the importance of standardized annotation protocols for model generalizability. This work contributes a scalable, non-invasive solution for early respiratory disease monitoring in calves, with potential to improve health outcomes and increase labor efficiency.

title: Automated sea cage geometry detection from 3D multibeam sonar using machine learning
abstract: Reliable interpretation of acoustic observations in aquaculture systems requires accurate knowledge of the spatial structure being monitored. In flexible sea cages, geometric deformation under varying hydrodynamic conditions alters the spatial reference frame used to analyse sensor data and can lead to errors in automated monitoring and analysis. This study presents an automated, data-driven approach for detecting sea cage geometry directly from 3D multibeam sonar observations collected at a commercial salmon farm. The approach combines time-synchronised acoustic measurements with physics-based simulation-derived reference geometries and trains a 3D convolutional neural network to infer cage geometry from sonar data alone. The final implementation was developed in PyTorch using supervised training on matched sonar–geometry pairs. Validation results show strong agreement between predicted and reference cage geometries, with overlap-based similarity values in the range of approximately 0.93–0.94. These results demonstrate that cage geometry can be inferred directly from sonar observations without relying on external deformation sensors during operation. The proposed method provides a non-invasive and scalable approach for real-time cage-scale monitoring and supports downstream applications such as fish behaviour analysis, biomass interpretation, and precision aquaculture decision support.

title: Autonomous construction of crop pest and disease knowledge graphs at scale via LLM-driven expert modeling
abstract: Crop pests and diseases pose a serious threat to global food security, which create an urgent need for rapid and accurate plant protection strategies. Much of the domain knowledge required for such intervention, however, remains scattered across heterogeneous and largely unstructured literature. This fragmentation limits the effective use of agricultural data in intelligent diagnosis and decision support, and it has increased the demand for high quality domain specific knowledge graphs. Existing approaches to agricultural knowledge graph construction still rely heavily on manual or partially automated curation, which restricts the efficient use of unstructured multi-source data and slows the incorporation of updated domain knowledge. To address these limitations, this study presents CropKG, an autonomous AI driven framework for reconstructing the knowledge engineering workflow in agricultural protection. Unlike conventional semi-automated approaches, CropKG integrates automated prompt engineering with expert oriented role modeling. By encoding agronomic reasoning patterns and combining them with bottom-up ontology induction, the framework supports autonomous extraction of complex entity relations from long agricultural documents while reducing unsupported generation in large language models. The effectiveness of the framework is demonstrated through the construction of a large-scale domain knowledge graph containing more than 17,000 nodes. Experimental results show that CropKG achieves an F1 score above 90% in entity and relation extraction and outperforms strong universal extraction baselines. The framework also supports decision-oriented applications by enabling traceable and evidence constrained retrieval of pest control knowledge. These results indicate that autonomous knowledge graph construction provides a practical path from raw agricultural text to structured and actionable intelligence for precision plant protection.

title: Quality-aware generative distillation for robust and efficient livestock detection
abstract: Vision-based livestock monitoring in open pastures confronts two distinct bottlenecks: a quality problem—severe image degradation from variable illumination (e.g., nighttime, strong snow reflection) yields abundant but low-quality frames—and a scarcity problem—extreme weather events (e.g., heavy snow, rain) are rare, leaving few training samples for such critical conditions. Generative image editors can in principle enhance degraded inputs and synthesize rare scenarios. However, unsupervised generation frequently introduces semantic artifacts and geometric distortions; naïvely incorporating these corrupted samples into training misleads detectors and degrades performance. To harness generative data reliably while meeting edge-device constraints, we propose a quality-aware generative distillation framework. First, a dual-branch editing pipeline—built on the large-scale instruction-driven editor Qwen-Image-Edit—restores visibility in low-quality inputs (enhancement branch) and simulates diverse adverse-weather views from clear daytime images (style-edit branch), addressing both quality and scarcity issues at the data level. Second, because generative outputs are unreliable, we design a multi-metric quality assessment module combining perceptual similarity (LPIPS), region-of-interest edge consistency, and CLIP-based semantic alignment to automatically filter corrupted edits before training. Third, to avoid deploying heavy generative models at inference, we train a robust teacher detector on this curated multi-domain dataset, then distill its localization features into a lightweight student via feature-level knowledge transfer; the student trains only on raw images, incurs no enhancement overhead at deployment, yet inherits cross-weather robustness. Experiments on our SnowLivestockDet dataset demonstrate that YOLOv11 and RT-DETR students achieve up to 12.5% mAP@50–95 improvement on adverse-weather subsets compared to single-domain baselines, validating the effectiveness of quality-aware generative distillation.

title: Semantic metadata extraction from crop model components with large language models to facilitate platform interoperability
abstract: Process-based crop models encapsulate agro-ecosystem knowledge in modular components, yet structural heterogeneity across platforms limits component reuse and demands manual curation of semantic metadata, which is error-prone and time consuming. Here, we present a workflow that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automatically create Crop2ML model specifications by extracting input/output variables specifications and by generating descriptions, from source code written in three different languages among six simulation platforms. Evaluation on eight soil temperature components from six widely used platforms and on 31 various components from three platforms showed F1-Score above 93% for input/output variables extraction. The workflow successfully inferred plausible metadata when documentation was ambiguous or incomplete. These findings demonstrate that LLM-assisted extraction can accelerate the creation of interoperable, semantically rich model documentation while preserving accuracy, thereby lowering the barrier to crop model reuse.

title: A generative compressed sensing-based method for reconstructing in-situ soil monitoring data
abstract: In-situ soil monitoring systems typically operate autonomously in field conditions, where hourly measurements consume substantial energy and accelerate equipment degradation. Compressed sensing (CS) can mitigate these issues through low-frequency sampling and subsequent reconstruction without sacrificing monitoring accuracy. In agricultural and environmental fields, however, standard CS methods are constrained by a theoretical minimum sampling ratio of 20% to 30%. Meanwhile, generative compressed sensing (GCS) methods, which hold promise for addressing this limitation through deep neural networks, remain insufficiently studied. This study proposes a GCS-CVAE method to achieve ultra-low frequency sampling in soil monitoring and establish a methodological foundation for the development of soil monitoring systems. This method utilizes the decoder of a high-latent-dimensional convolutional variational autoencoder (CVAE) as a data reconstructor, coupled with a multiple-optimization strategy derived from GCS mechanism analysis. Experimental results on a soil moisture content (SMC) dataset demonstrate that GCS-CVAE outperforms existing CS and deep learning methods in both accuracy and stability. Notably, it can reconstruct hourly SMC series at highly reduced sampling rates of 10% and 15%, achieving average R2 values that exceed 0.8 and 0.9, respectively. For future deployment, GCS-CVAE can be integrated with wireless sensor networks or the Internet of Things via asynchronous sampling and multi-node collaboration to alleviate temporal feature loss during sparse sampling.

title: A computer vision driven ecosystem for cattle monitoring: Multi-disease classification with severity grading, multi-view individual identification, and weight estimation
abstract: This study introduces a computer vision based cattle monitoring ecosystem, which (i) performs multi-disease classification and severity grading with 85.88% hierarchical accuracy, (ii) achieves multi-view cattle identification with 89.80% Rank-5 accuracy under cross-view-angle and domain shift conditions, and (iii) estimates body weight from four view RGB images and metadata with an MAE of 35.10 kg, developed using custom-collected, curated datasets combined with publicly available datasets. For the disease module, a hierarchical cross-attentional multi-task architecture classifies Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD), Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD), Infectious Bovine Keratoconjunctivitis (IBK), and Healthy cattle, while grading diseased cases into Stage-1 (mild), Stage-2 (moderate), and Stage-3 (severe) using clinically graded veterinarian supervised annotations, achieving 89.96% disease classification accuracy, 83.75% severity staging accuracy, and 85.88% hierarchical accuracy (disease → severity). On a custom collected dataset, YOLOv8s localizes cattle from left, right, front, and back views with an IoU of 0.93 and mAP@0.5 of 0.97, providing the basis for identification and weight estimation. Multi-view individual cattle identification achieves Rank-1 accuracies of 96.40% (Rank-5: 100%) under Leave-One-View-Out evaluation and 74.56% (Rank-5: 89.80%) under cross-view-angle and domain-shift testing using ConvNeXt-Tiny. In weight estimation module, ensemble learning over multi-view images and metadata achieves an MAE of 35.10 kg. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of an affordable, low-shot, non-invasive RGB-based system for disease diagnosis with severity grading, multi-view cattle identification, and practical live-weight estimation without invasive sensors.

title: Wind-excited audio-based leaf area density estimation in apple-tree canopies: Mechanism-guided generative denoising and attention-based spectrogram learning
abstract: Leaf area density (LAD) describes canopy compactness in apple orchards and supports variable-rate spraying decisions. However, real-time in-field LAD sensing remains challenging because occlusion, illumination variability, and strong equipment noise reduce the reliability and learnability of canopy observations. This study proposes a mechanism-guided wind-excited acoustic sensing framework for LAD grade estimation in apple-tree canopies. First, mechanism-based analysis was used to identify the dominant noise sources and key frequency bands, and passive noise reduction was adopted to improve acquisition consistency. Then, a correlation-mean-square-error (MSE) constrained deep neural network (CM-DNN) was used to reconstruct low-SNR wind-excited audio. Finally, a spectral-centroid statistical prior was introduced to guide frequency-axis attention, and a spectral-centroid attention deep convolutional neural network (SCA-DCNN) model was used to classify log-power spectrum spectrograms. The results showed that passive noise reduction decreased device background noise from 72.7 dB to 65.4 dB, and 10 m/s was selected as the unified acquisition condition. On this basis, SCA-DCNN improved accuracy by 3.50 percentage points over the baseline DCNN and achieved 91.50 % accuracy on independent field samples. Overall, the proposed combination of mechanism-guided noise control, low-SNR signal reconstruction, and prior-guided attention improved the learnability of orchard acoustic data and provided a deployable sensing pathway for prescription-oriented canopy grading.

title: Enhancing soil organic matter prediction by Decoupling soil moisture effects with a conditional generative adversarial network
abstract: Soil moisture significantly affects soil spectral reflectance, and its high variability severely undermines the accuracy of soil organic matter (SOM) prediction. To address this issue, soil samples were collected from northern and northeastern China to construct three independent datasets. A deep generative model, Wet Spectrum to Dry Spectrum (Wet2dry) was then developed to capture the structural characteristics of one-dimensional spectral features. On this basis, three moisture-correction methods—Direct Standardization (DS), External Parameter Orthogonalization (EPO), and Wet2dry—with three SOM prediction models: Random Forest, Transformer, and SE-Transformer were systematically compared. Results show that the Wet2dry method effectively eliminates moisture interference and improves SOM prediction accuracy, offering a robust solution for soil property spectral inversion under high moisture variability. In SOM prediction tasks, the SE-Transformer model, which integrates the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism, exhibited stronger responsiveness to critical spectral bands. When combined with the Wet2dry correction model, the SE-Transformer consistently achieved excellent prediction performance across different moisture levels (5%, 10%, 15%), with R2 > 0.75 and RPD > 2. This study extends image-generation network architectures to one-dimensional spectral modeling, providing a feasible solution for stable SOM prediction under moisture interference.

title: DELKNet + LLM: lightweight multi-model integration real-time perception and pre decision analysis for facility tomato
abstract: Precise phenotypic perception and reliable decision-making are critical for the intelligent management of greenhouse tomatoes. However, existing methods often lack an integrated closed-loop “perception-to-reasoning” workflow and struggle with high computational costs on edge devices. This study proposes PP-LLMs, an innovative framework that bridges visual perception and agronomic reasoning by integrating a lightweight detection model, YOLON, with a fine-tuned Large Language Model, Tomato-Qwen. Our core contributions are threefold. First, we constructed the TGMD (Tomato Growth Multimodal Dataset), a benchmark comprising 9,519 high-quality expert-annotated language pairs covering descriptions of tomato growth status and agricultural production knowledge.Second, we developed YOLON, which employs efficient DELK-Block and GSLK modules to achieve high-precision detection of tomato organs while maintaining a lightweight architecture suitable for real-time edge deployment. Third, by applying a two-stage fine-tuning process (LoRA and prompt learning) to Qwen-7B-Chat, we enabled Tomato-Qwen to perform complex agronomic reasoning based on real-time phenotypic and environmental data. Experimental results demonstrate that this strategy significantly outperforms mainstream baselines. Tomato-Qwen achieved substantial improvements in QA tasks, with BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L scores increasing by 29.42% and 33.13% respectively.This research demonstrates the preliminary effectiveness of visual-language collaboration in agriculture and suggests a potentially scalable solution for autonomous greenhouse management. But the generated agronomic suggestions should be regarded as preliminary candidate outputs whose practical safety and reliability have not yet been validated by domain experts.

title: FedAD: Federated learning with generative data augmentation and adaptive parameter decomposition for rice pest and disease identification
abstract: Rice is a primary global food source, but its production is severely threatened by pests and diseases, leading to significant yield losses and economic instability. Traditional manual identification is labor-intensive and error-prone. Deep Learning (DL) offers automated and accurate diagnosis, but its centralized deployment raises data privacy concerns and incurs high communication costs. Federated Learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving alternative, but it faces challenges such as statistical heterogeneity (Non-IID data) and stringent resource constraints in the Internet of Agricultural Things (IoAT). To address these issues, we propose a personalized framework called Adaptive Parameter Decomposition Federated Learning (FedAD). FedAD employs a strategy based on Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to decouple model weights into a shared full-rank component and a personalized low-rank component, and we introduce a dynamic rank allocation mechanism to adaptively adjust the personalized capacity for each client without requiring explicit SVD decomposition. In addition, we design a resource-efficient backbone model (SepResNet) to balance model performance with overall resource constraints in federated environments. To mitigate data scarcity and improve robustness, we construct a novel dataset (RP15) by employing a hybrid augmentation strategy that combines traditional transformations with generative AI synthesis. Experiments on both the RP15 dataset and the public PlantVillage dataset demonstrate the superior performance and generalization ability of FedAD. On the RP15 dataset, FedAD achieves 90.40% Accuracy, an 86.79% F1-Score, and 87.10% Recall, outperforming baseline methods by over 10% and doubling the convergence speed. On the PlantVillage dataset, FedAD achieves 99.45% Accuracy, a 99.04% F1-Score, and 99.12% Recall, significantly outperforming baseline models. Finally, we provide both experimental and theoretical validation of the framework’s convergence, which ensures training stability and offers guidance for hyperparameter selection. The source code and RP15 dataset are available at https://github.com/DongfuHou/FedAD.

title: Toward intelligent pig farming: Advancing health and welfare monitoring through computer vision–based behavioral analysis
abstract: Modern pig production is increasingly moving toward smart and intelligent farming systems, integrating advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence for precision management. Camera-based computer vision has emerged as a promising non-contact sensing tool for monitoring pig health and welfare through behavioral analysis, given the strong association between behavioral patterns and physiological status. Following a PRISMA-based search, 45 studies were included for critical synthesis on computer vision-based behavioral analysis in pigs, with emphasis on detectable behavioral indicators, imaging configurations, model architectures, post-processing strategies, and deployment constraints. Findings show that posture and nutritive behaviors are the most mature targets for monitoring because they are visually distinctive, biologically informative, and compatible with lightweight object-detection pipelines. In contrast, aggression, biting, enrichment interaction, suckling, and individual activity metrics require stronger temporal modeling, segmentation, or multi-object tracking, which increases annotation burden, computational cost, and susceptibility to occlusion and identity errors. Recent pig-specific modifications to YOLO, transformer-inspired, segmentation, and tracking models have improved performance through attention mechanisms, multi-scale feature fusion, occlusion-aware regression, lightweight convolution, and detector-tracker coupling. However, high reported accuracies often reflect controlled datasets rather than commercial robustness. Critical barriers include limited multi-farm validation, inconsistent annotation and post-processing rules, insufficient anomaly-detection thresholds, weak long-term identity preservation, and hardware constraints for edge deployment. Future efforts should prioritize developing standardized benchmarks, biologically grounded behavioral metrics, explainable and domain-adaptive artificial intelligence, and edge-ready architectures that convert model outputs into interpretable management alerts. This review provides a deployment-oriented framework for advancing computer vision from experimental behavior recognition toward scalable behavioral monitoring and intelligent decision support in pig production systems.

title: AquaAgent-OSPy: an auditable LLM tool-agent system for simulation-grounded irrigation decision support
abstract: Irrigation scheduling in agricultural water management requires balancing crop yield, water efficiency, and safety constraints under inter-annual rainfall variability. Existing approaches − fixed irrigation calendars, numerical optimizers, and conversational AI advisors − share a common gap: they do not deliver model-grounded recommendations that are simultaneously traceable, safety-checked, and adaptive to climate conditions. AquaAgent-OSPy is an A4-class code-executing large language model (LLM) tool-agent that orchestrates AquaCrop-OSPy irrigation scenario simulations, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) multi-objective optimization, Google Earth Engine (GEE) site context verification, and an illustrative seasonal-irrigation safety checker to generate auditable action memos with full tool provenance. The system was evaluated at two confirmed Korean paddy rice sites (Gimje, Jeollabuk-do and Hampyeong, Jeollanam-do) across three contrasting climate years (403–824 mm May-September growing-season precipitation) using a five-item binary faithfulness rubric (F1-F5). As a pilot unit-audit of memo traceability, not a statistical reliability estimate for LLM behavior, four confirmed-site action memos passed all rubric items (20/20 combined). The evaluation produced four findings: (1) the GEE land-cover and Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) pipeline caught an automated site-selection error and confirmed paddy rice phenology at both sites; (2) in a severe drought year (2015, 403 mm), the fixed weekly schedule triggered the illustrative high-irrigation safety flag (239 mm > 200 mm) and achieved lower water productivity (WP) than the selected low-irrigation threshold strategy under shared AquaCrop-OSPy assumptions; (3) across all four primary evaluation cases, the agent recommended soil-moisture threshold (SMT) scheduling or zero irrigation and never recommended a safety-flagged strategy, while scenario results from all six case-year combinations supported the same within-model water-saving advisory pattern; (4) AquaCrop-OSPy PaddyRice outputs were qualitatively aligned with a published Thailand site (Veerakachen and Raksapatcharawong, 2020; rainfed yield 4.77 t/ha within a reported 3–5 t/ha range), providing a plausibility check rather than Korean field validation. Soil hydraulic parameters were cross-checked against SoilGrids v2.0. AquaAgent-OSPy is intended for agronomist review: it links recommendations to simulation outputs and safety checks, but it does not authorize or actuate irrigation.

title: Adaptive feature learning and wavelet preservation for forest canopy mapping from UAV imagery
abstract: Accurate forest canopy cover mapping serves as a fundamental support for forest resource inventory, ecosystem management and carbon sink accounting. The integration of ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery and convolutional neural networks has advanced the efficiency of forest canopy extraction. Nevertheless, current approaches still encounter limitations when applied to scenes with complex backgrounds and dense forest conditions, particularly in accurate canopy boundary delineation and fine-grained target discrimination. Such limitations are primarily attributed to insufficient adaptive modeling of canopy geometric and textural characteristics, as well as the loss of critical structural details during downsampling. This work presents GMNet, a dedicated network for forest canopy mapping, which consists of two core modules, namely Gradient Adaptive Dynamic Convolution and Multi-scale Wavelet Range Downsampling. The Gradient Adaptive Dynamic Convolution module adaptively recalibrates convolutional kernel weights based on gradient cues to facilitate effective canopy feature learning in complex scenarios. The Multi-scale Wavelet Range Downsampling module integrates multi-scale wavelet decomposition with distance statistics to preserve essential structural characteristics, especially boundary details, throughout the downsampling procedure. Evaluated on the BAMFORESTS benchmark dataset, GMNet achieves competitive performance against several state-of-the-art remote sensing segmentation models across commonly adopted metrics. The presented model also maintains comparatively stable performance under changing illumination conditions and canopy shadow interference. The proposed approach is capable of supporting reliable canopy extraction in dense forest scenarios with complex illumination and overlapping tree crowns, showing applicability for forest resource assessment and sustainable forest management. The code is available at https://github.com/WangShiK/GMNet.

title: Agri-CPJ: A training-free explainable framework for agricultural pest diagnosis using Caption-Prompt-Judge and LLM-as-a-Judge
abstract: Crop disease diagnosis from field photographs faces two recurring problems: models that score well on benchmarks frequently hallucinate species names, and when predictions are correct, the reasoning behind them is typically inaccessible to the practitioner. This paper describes Agri-CPJ (Caption-Prompt-Judge), a training-free few-shot framework in which a large vision-language model first generates a structured morphological caption, quality-gated and, when triggered, refined once, before any diagnostic question is answered. Two candidate responses are then generated from complementary viewpoints, and an LLM judge selects the stronger one based on domain-specific criteria. The ablations show that introducing a caption at all, even before any quality refinement, is the single largest contributor to downstream accuracy for both models tested; quality-gated refinement of that caption adds a smaller but systematic further increment. On CDDMBench, the full caption-enhanced pipeline yields +22.7 pp in disease classification and +19.5 points in QA score over no-caption baselines (GPT-5-Nano with GPT-5-mini caption generator), with ablations showing caption introduction accounts for the majority of the gain. Evaluated without modification on AgMMU-MCQs, GPT-5-Nano reached 77.84% and Qwen-VL-Chat reached 64.54%, placing them at or above most open-source models of comparable scale despite the format shift from open-ended to multiple-choice. The structured caption and judge rationale together constitute a readable intermediate record: a practitioner who disagrees with a diagnosis can inspect the specific caption observation the answer was conditioned on, though we make no claim that the judge’s written rationale is a faithful account of the computation that produced its selection. The code and scripts are publicly available.11https://github.com/CPJ-Agricultural/CPJ-Agricultural-Diagnosis.

title: Lightweight autonomous construction and application of a knowledge graph for soil acidification constraint management based on LLM agents
abstract: In the red and yellow soil regions of southern China, long-term practices in soil acidification constraint management have revealed several challenges, including fragmented knowledge systems, high technical thresholds, and pronounced regional disparities in technical capacity, which collectively hinder the systematic integration and dissemination of management experience. To address these limitations, this study proposes a lightweight autonomous construction framework for a knowledge graph of soil acidification management based on large language model (LLM) agents. By introducing an "AI associative matrix" and a semantic expansion-retrieval mechanism, the framework enables the system to automatically infer related concepts and relationships from a small set of domain-specific keywords, thereby generating an initial ontology structure and knowledge graph schema for management tasks. In addition, a network protocol-based control strategy is incorporated to semantically parse publicly available governmental reports and monitoring data, facilitating automated processes such as entity recognition and relation extraction. At the system implementation level, a cloud-edge collaborative lightweight architecture is adopted to reduce computational requirements and improve usability. Through an empirical in-situ deployment and lightweight field-level testing conducted directly at the farm sites of Chengmai County, Hainan Province, this framework demonstrated a robust capacity to adapt to users with different technical backgrounds and regions with varying levels of resource input, while providing extensibility for the continuous integration of emerging technologies and updated policy regulations. Overall, this study offers a lightweight, user-friendly, and scalable intelligent approach for cultivated land quality improvement and agricultural ecological management.

title: Dual-branch frequency-domain fusion for RGB-D tree trunks instance segmentation
abstract: Tree trunk instance segmentation is a crucial task in vision-based perception systems for forestry robots, enabling precise autonomous navigation in complex forest environments. However, existing RGB-only methods struggle to achieve adequate accuracy due to challenges such as uneven illumination and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, we propose TrunkInst, a dual-branch, frequency-domain fusion RGB-D network for tree trunk instance segmentation. TrunkInst employs a Frequency-Domain Decomposition Gate Fusion (FDGF) module that decomposes and selectively fuses RGB and depth features in the frequency domain, enhancing segmentation accuracy by suppressing noise and preserving important details. The Multi-Head Dynamic Upsampling (MDU) module generates higher-quality upsampled feature maps by learning multiple offset groups, improving the resolution of small tree trunks. Finally, a Transformer decoder, using cross-modal queries between RGB features and fused representations, mitigates the negative effects of degraded depth maps. We also propose the Trunk-Depths dataset, which includes 1,326 finely annotated RGB-depth image pairs for tree-trunk instance segmentation. On this dataset, TrunkInst achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 52.8%, with 85.3% AP at IoU=0.5 and 54.4% AP at IoU=0.75—improvements of +2.6%, +1.4%, and +4.6% over an RGB baseline, respectively. Further experiments on the public COME15K and NYU-Depth-V2 datasets demonstrate the generality and robustness of the model. TrunkInst also delivers real-time inference at 45 fps, achieving a good trade-off between accuracy and speed.

title: EPDNet: A method for identifying tomato leaf diseases with uneven samples
abstract: Tomato industry is one of the important parts of agriculture, and the timely diagnosis of leaf diseases plays a key role in ensuring its production safety. At present, most of the mainstream recognition technologies are based on laboratory standard images to construct recognition models. Although they can achieve accurate analysis of isolated leaves, it is difficult to cope with the practical challenges such as complex climate and environmental factors of plant growth in open environments. The recognition is difficult due to the influence factors of open environment, such as the distortion of disease spots caused by light, the occlusion of branches and leaves, and the confusion of soil attachment and real disease spots. To solve the problem of unbalanced distribution of tomato leaf disease samples in open environment and the big difference of similar diseases, this study proposes a single-modal recognition architecture for tomato leaf diseases based on Efficient localization and Physical information and Dynamic adaptive optimization Network (EPDNet). Firstly, an efficient positioning feature enhancement module is designed to effectively enhance the network’s attention to important regions by calculating and fusing the horizontal and vertical attention weights. Then, a physical information neural network-cross entropy hybrid loss function was designed to ensure the accuracy of prediction, while restricting the smoothness and continuity of the feature map to improve the robustness of the model. Finally, a dynamic adaptive optimization algorithm was designed to iteratively update the learning rate to improve the feature discrimination ability, so as to reduce the identification differences of diseases within the class. Experimental results show that the accuracy of EPDNet on the tomato leaf dataset reaches 93.62%, and the F1 score reaches 93.31 %, which is significantly better than the existing methods. This study provides an effective solution for the application of deep learning methods in crop diseases.

title: Diagnosis of maize nitrogen status under contrasting water and nitrogen regimes using a canopy-stratified and multi-source remote sensing framework
abstract: Maize leaf nitrogen exhibits significant vertical heterogeneity within the canopy, which often compromises the accuracy of remote sensing-based nitrogen status diagnosis. To address the limited consideration of leaf-layer contributions and multi-source feature integration, this study proposed a three-dimensional coupled nitrogen diagnosis framework integrating progressive leaf-layer labeling, multi-source feature fusion, and machine learning modeling, based on spring maize experiments under various water and nitrogen regimes in Xinjiang, China. Stratified ground sampling was conducted to obtain leaf nitrogen weight (LNW) from the upper, middle, and lower canopy layers, and 22 vegetation indices (VIs), eight texture features (TFs), and 15 texture indices (TIs) were extracted from UAV multispectral imagery to construct a multi-source feature set. Results demonstrated that the combination of upper and middle canopy leaves best represented overall plant nitrogen status. Feature fusion significantly enhanced model performance, with extreme gradient boosting achieving the highest estimation accuracy for the nitrogen nutrition index (NNI) (R2 = 0.68, RPD = 1.77), and convolutional neural networks performing best in LNW estimation (R2 = 0.83, RPD = 2.31). The critical nitrogen dilution curves derived from the estimated LNW revealed that irrigation levels significantly influenced the curve intercepts and slopes, highlighting the dual regulatory effects of water on nitrogen uptake and dilution. Coupled with ArcGIS-based spatial visualization, the framework enabled dynamic monitoring of NNI across V6, VT, R3, and R6 growth stages. Overall, this framework effectively improved both the spatiotemporal resolution and estimation accuracy of maize nitrogen status, providing a theoretical basis and technical support for precision nitrogen management and the transition toward sustainable agriculture.

title: A multi-scale linear cross-modal fusion architecture for tomato leaf disease segmentation
abstract: Tomato, as a globally important economic crop, requires precise and timely disease management to secure yield and quality. Yet segmentation robustness is often limited by weak semantic understanding from single-modality images, narrow receptive fields of convolutional structures, and discontinuous boundary predictions. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-scale Linear Cross-modal Fusion Architecture for Tomato Leaf Disease Segmentation (MS-LCFNet). We construct a real-world field dataset covering five major tomato leaf diseases, annotated by experts with detailed textual descriptions to enable multimodal learning. MS-LCFNet strengthens semantic representation via cross-modal fusion, captures local and global context through an Adaptive Long-short Distance Perception module, and improves boundary continuity with a Physics-informed Smoothness-constrained Loss. Experiments show that MS-LCFNet achieves 87.13 % mIoU on our dataset and 90.78 % on PlantVillage, improving over previous state-of-the-art methods by + 4.62 % and + 4.48 %, respectively, and demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness in complex agricultural scenarios.

title: AdaFishCount: Advancing domain-invariant learning via domain-specific perturbation for cross-domain fish counting
abstract: Deep learning-based fish counting is crucial for intelligent aquaculture management. However, variations in water transparency, fish distribution, and camera perspectives introduce significant domain gaps, limiting the adaptability of data-driven counting methods across diverse real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, an unsupervised domain adaptation framework, named AdaFishCount, is designed for fish counting. AdaFishCount integrates domain-specific feature perturbation and domain-invariant feature learning. Specifically, the Domain-Specific Feature Perturbation (DSFP) module performs controllable perturbations in the source feature space to generate target-style samples, simulating domain shifts between different aquaculture environments. Subsequently, domain-invariant feature learning leverages an Attention-guided Domain-Invariant Selector (ADIS) and a Long-term Domain-Invariant Memory (LDIM) module to extract stable and discriminative fish representations. Moreover, a comprehensive loss function is devised to ensure consistent density distributions under various style perturbations and to enhance focus on domain-invariant features. Experimental results demonstrate that AdaFishCount achieves superior cross-domain performance, notably improving MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 14.66, 15.24, and 43.96, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art method on the target domain Tank 2, highlighting its strong robustness to domain gaps.

title: FM-SAM: individual tree crown delineation and classification based on Segmentation Anything Model (SAM) and YOLOv10 in UAV imagery for forest monitoring
abstract: Forest monitoring plays a crucial role in the sustainable management and conservation of natural resources, with tree crown delineation being a key task for assessing forest structure and tree health. This study presents a novel framework, FM-SAM, integrating YOLOv10 and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for precise tree crown segmentation and species identification in UAV imagery. The framework combines YOLOv10’s real-time detection capabilities with SAM’s strong segmentation, significantly improving segmentation and classification accuracy. SAM is also employed as a semi-supervised branch in FM-SAM to expedite the annotation process, offering a solution that reduces the need for extensive manual labeling. Experimental results on the MixedForestDataset , comprising both coniferous and broadleaf tree species, demonstrate that FM-SAM outperforms traditional deep learning frameworks such as DeepLabv3 and YOLO-based models, achieving high accuracy, precision, and recall values. The proposed method excels in complex forest environments, enhancing the effectiveness of tree crown delineation and classification for large-scale forest monitoring applications. • FM-SAM framework merges YOLOv10 and SAM for high-accuracy tree crown segmentation. • Efficient labeling with Semi-Supervised Approach, making MixedForestDataset . • The brightness of the images is correlated with the segmentation accuracy.

title: Enhancing poultry multi-behavior detection with semi-supervised auto-labeling and prompt-driven zero-shot recognition
abstract: The poultry industry faces growing challenges in ensuring animal welfare, preventing disease outbreaks, and addressing labor shortages. Traditional vision intelligence-based behavior monitoring needs intensive manual labeling, which is impractical for large-scale operations, necessitating advanced, efficient, and scalable solutions. Therefore, this study explores a novel label-efficient learning approach that integrates semi-supervised and text-prompt-based zero-shot learning to enhance poultry behavior detection. Furthermore, the study introduced a dataset that includes 11 common poultry behaviors essential for monitoring to improve health, welfare, and productivity. A dataset comprising 200 annotated images (I-200) with 3,870 instances and 640 annotated images (I-640) with 14,552 instances was utilized for both supervised and semi-supervised training. Additionally, 2,500 unannotated images were incorporated to enhance the model’s performance through semi-supervised learning. This research aims to fully utilize the dataset, facilitate behavior monitoring, and support data-driven decision-making in poultry management by developing and refining an auto-labeling model using an active learning technique. The integration of prompt-then-detect zero-shot models (Clip, GDINO, and YOLOWorld) with a user-friendly text-based detection system further enhances the performance of the semi-supervised model. The results of this study demonstrated that the YOLOv9s model outperformed other supervised learning models, achieving strong performance metrics with a precision of 81.1 %, a recall of 77.9 %, and an F1-score of 79.5 %. With that as the starting point, the semi-supervised I-640 model, which utilized 2,500 pseudo-labeled images, achieved 86.9 % precision, 84.3 % recall, and an 84.9 % F1-score, outperforming all other supervised and semi-supervised baselines. This model improved performance by more than 4.6 % in precision compared to supervised model validation, but also achieved improvements of 5.8 %, 6.4 %, and 5.4 % in precision, recall, and F1-score for prediction results. Furthermore, the trained semi-supervised I-640 model with the integration of YOLOWorld text-prompt feature showed further performance improvements. This text prompt not only helps to detect specific behaviors but also assists users to easy auto-label images. This enhancement can significantly reduce manual annotation efforts and supporting timely intervention. These findings highlight the potential of AI-driven approaches for precision poultry monitoring, offering a scalable and efficient solution for sustainable poultry farming.

title: CSLTSM-Net: A lightweight two-stream mixed neural network for chicken sound recognition
abstract: Monitoring the physiological state and behavior of poultry during breeding was of great significance for the welfare and intelligent development of poultry breeding. Poultry audio contained a large amount of physiological state and behavioral activity information. Driven by the development of artificial intelligence, computer auditory monitoring of poultry based on machine learning has attracted more attention by researchers. This paper introduced CSLTSM-Net, a lightweight two-stream mixed neural network designed for processing chicken sounds. The aim was to explore deep learning applications in poultry physiological state and behavior monitoring. First, teacher-model convolutional neural network (TMCNN) and teacher-model time-series neural network (TMTSNN) for chicken sound recognition with complex structure and many training parameters were constructed. After training, both models demonstrated strong abilities to recognize poultry feeding sounds (99.75 % accuracy in TMCNN and 95.25 % accuracy in TMTSNN). Second, student-model convolutional neural network (SMCNN) and student-model time-series neural network (SMTSNN) with simple structure and few training parameters were constructed, and both student models were trained using their corresponding teacher models. Finally, SMCNN and SMTSNN model were mixed together to form a lightweight two-stream neural network CSLTSM-Net. The experimental results showed that the performance of the student model trained by the teacher model was higher than that directly trained by the original training set. SMCNN with teacher training achieved 96.25 % accuracy, 94.69 % specificity, 97.93 % recall, 94.5 % precision and 96.18 % F1-score in the test set. SMTSNN with teacher training achieved 94.25 % accuracy, 95.79 % specificity, 91.55 % recall, 96.06 % precision and 93.75 % F1-score in the test set. SMCNN with original dataset training achieved 95.75 % accuracy, 94.2 % specificity, 97.4 % recall, 94 % precision and 95.67 % F1-score in the test set. SMTSNN with original training set achieved 91.75 % accuracy, 93.72 % specificity, 89.95 % recall, 94 % precision and 91.93 % F1-score in the test set. The proposed CSLTSM-Net achieved 97 % accuracy, 97 % specificity, 97 % recall, 97 % precision and 97 % F1-score in the test set. Compared with SMCNN and SMTSNN alone, the overall performance was better. The lightweight two-stream mixed neural network could be compressed to a large extent at the cost of a small amount of recognition performance, which is conducive to solving the problem that the direct use of deep neural networks with complex structure and numerous parameters was not conducive to embedding in the miniaturized low-cost equipment with small storage capacity and weak computing power in poultry farms.

title: Routing enabled optimization and deep recurrent VGG-16 model for plant disease detection in IoT
abstract: Agricultural productivity is the major source of the economy of the agrarian nation and is also considered the major source of human activities. It is vital to detect and manage plant diseases to enhance the overall growth and quality of agricultural produce. Modern agriculture increasingly uses IoT and automation tools to monitor and collect valuable information on plant health and disease occurrence. Here, the plant disease is detected using Deep Recurrent Visual Geometry Group-16 (DRVGG-16) in the IoT platform with routing based on the Adam Dung Beetle Optimization (ADBO) algorithm. The DRVGG-16 is the combination of Deep Recurrent Neural Network (DRNN) with Visual Geometry Group-16 (VGG-16) and ADBO is the fusion of Adam optimizer with Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO). Initially, the captured agricultural images are transmitted to the base station via ADBO-optimized routing for plant disease detection. The base station initiates disease detection by applying a bilateral filter to preprocess the input plant leaf images. The preprocessed images are segmented using the DeepLabV3+ model, and features are subsequently derived from the segmented leaf areas. Finally, plant disease detection is performed using the proposed DRVGG-16 model. Furthermore, the performances of the proposed schemes are validated, where ADBO attained distance, delay and energy of 0.343 m, 0.305 ms and 0.375 J. The DRVGG-16 obtained superior results of 91.43 % accuracy, 90.63 % True Positive Rate (TPR), 90.73 % precision, 92.34 % True Negative Rate (TNR) and 90.68 % F1-score. Therefore, the proposed IoT-based framework combining DRVGG-16 and ADBO routing effectively detects plant diseases with high accuracy while optimizing energy and transmission efficiency.

title: Towards damage-less robotic fragile fruit grasping: Learning adaptive grasping force from multimodal data and human demonstration
abstract: In fruit postharvest industry, uploading and packaging involve continuous manual pick-and-place. We aim to replace manual work with robotic grasping. However, to achieve robotic fragile fruit grasping, the main difficulty is to reduce early stage bruise while maintaining grasping reliability. For pneumatic-driven soft gripper and fragile fruit with diversities in size, shape, weight, firmness, and ripeness, how to grasp with adaptive and closed-loop controlled grasping force is still a problem that deserves to be studied. In this study, we propose a multimodal gasping framework inspired by the human pinching and pre-grasping behavior to solve this problem, which contains a neural network that could learn adaptive grasping force (LAFNet) from human demonstration. The designed LAFNet takes both tactile modality and air pressure modality during robotic pinching as input. And adopts Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and transformer architectures to extract local, sequential, and global features, respectively. The trained LAFNet could predict adaptive grasping force for the current pinching fruit within 1.20 ms. Ablation studies were carried out to obtain the best structure of the LAFNet, the effectiveness of the multimodal input and fusion strategy was also validated on different kinds of fragile fruit. The adaptive grasping force estimation error was 0.82 ± 0.71 N on all experimental fruit. Finally, the performance of the grasping framework was also evaluated through extensive experiments. In all, this study provides a feasible solution for damage-less robotic fragile fruit grasping. Code: https://github.com/wangqingyu985/LAFNet. Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TA4_WcDDMHQ&t=10s&ab_channel=QingyuWang.

title: Underwater Near-Infrared image reconstruction for nighttime fish hypoxia monitoring
abstract: Hypoxia induced by low dissolved oxygen levels represents a significant challenge to fish health in recirculating aquaculture systems, especially at night when human intervention is limited. Employing computer vision technology to analyze behavioral changes in fish offers a low-cost and efficient method for hypoxia monitoring. However, existing monitoring methods are mainly designed for daytime use and require continuous artificial lighting at night, potentially disrupt the natural circadian rhythms of fish. To achieve non-intrusive nighttime hypoxia monitoring, this study proposes a novel method based on underwater near-infrared (NIR) image reconstruction. This method is centered on three core image reconstruction submodules based on autoencoder and generative adversarial network (GAN) architectures: brightness equalization, low-brightness reconstruction, and super-resolution modules. These submodules transform low-resolution nighttime underwater NIR images into high-resolution images with normal brightness, enabling consistent hypoxia monitoring around the clock. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method enhances monitoring accuracy during nighttime, reducing false positives and negatives. Its unique architecture supports a pipeline parallel strategy, improving inference speed to approximately 10 fps.

title: Dynamic prediction of carbon and nitrogen accumulation in winter wheat grain: Source-sink theory integrated with UAV multispectral imagery
abstract: Timely monitoring of grain carbon and nitrogen accumulation dynamics is crucial for the growth monitoring and efficient field management of winter wheat. However, traditional destructive sampling methods are time-consuming, costly, and challenging to implement for large-scale rapid monitoring.
