Our comparative study reveals that, out of the seven machine learning models evaluated, the deep neural network (DNN) exhibits the highest accuracy in estimating fresh weight, coupled with the strongest model stability and cross-variety applicability. For the DNN and extra trees (ET) models with relatively superior performance, we implement the Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) algorithms to quantitatively analyze the impact of input features on the models. The results indicate that agronomic traits contribute more to the estimation results compared to image features, and the number of leaves is the most dominant factor. The framework is capable of identifying the dominant factors influencing the model’s output, providing not only highly accurate estimations but also enhancing the understanding of the model’s decision making.

title: Multimodal deep learning framework for robust individual identification of Holstein cattle using gait dynamics and coat pattern features
abstract: Accurate individual cattle identification is critical for precision livestock farming. Some of the challenges associated with identification in the outdoor farm environment include factors such as variable illumination, mud contamination, and frequent occlusions, which often degrade the quality of visual features, limiting the reliability of existing identification methods. Given the lack of specificity to identify and track uniform-colored cattle in outdoor environments using existing methods, this study presents a deep learning framework that integrates gait dynamics and coat pattern features to reliably identify Holstein cattle. Using ground-based video data capturing 54 cows, developed was the framework that employs structural similarity index −based gait cycle segmentation, a CNN-BiLSTM network with attention (FCANet) for gait feature extraction, and an AlexNet-based model for occlusion mitigated pattern recognition. A dynamic decision-level fusion strategy (gait-pattern weighting: 4:6 for patterned and 7:3 for patternless cows) enhances cattle identification accuracy. The framework achieved 96.76% Rank-1 accuracy for patterned cows and 92.15% for patternless ones, with dynamic fusion improving performance by 2.24%. Framework maintained 88.12% mAP for lame cattle, though health transitions affected feature consistency. Error analysis highlighted challenges from cattle head turning behaviour and environmental factors like structural shadows and mud on the cattle. Overall, the study developed a multimodal approach to address key limitations of unimodal biometrics, offering a practical solution for cow identification in heterogeneous cattle populations under farm conditions.

title: Multi-view multi-task deep neural network for effective tea classification and quantitative flavor factor evaluation
abstract: Rapid and accurate evaluation of tea quality using artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms is crucial for effective quality management. Existing algorithms primarily focus on one-dimensional data (typically the appearance of dry tea) for classification or grading, often overlooking the complexity of tea flavor. Here, we developed Tea MvMtNet, a multi-view, multi-task deep neural network that processes visual data from dry tea appearance, infusion color, and waste tea to assess all five flavor factors, including taste and aroma, and to classify teas into distinct categories. The model incorporates an attention-enhanced bidirectional feature pyramid network for multi-scale fusion, extracting both global and local details from each view. The semantic enhancement module incorporates prior knowledge, leveraging cross-modal attention and graph attention networks to refine visual features for accurate prediction of flavor factors. Additionally, the multi-view fusion dynamically aggregates the three visual features to predict aroma, taste, and tea category. To optimize task performance and address data imbalance, we develop a multi-task balanced focal regression loss function for multi-task learning. Our approach achieved a classification accuracy of 98.11% and demonstrated superior precision in evaluating dry tea appearance (average absolute error percentage: 19.60%), infusion color (28.40%), aroma (26.48%), taste (31.67%), waste tea (17.20%), and overall score (17.23%), demonstrating that the accuracy of the model was comparable to that of senior tea evaluators. Furthermore, the overall score achieved an R2 value of 0.8359, with the best performance for aroma and taste (R2 > 0.75). These results highlight Tea MvMtNet as a comprehensive and precise tool for automated tea quality management.

title: A machine learning approach with SHAP interpretation for predicting fruit inertial force in vibration harvesting of Camellia oleifera
abstract: Vibration harvesting is an effective approach for the mechanized harvesting of Camellia oleifera fruit. Accurate prediction of fruit inertial force is crucial for enhancing harvesting efficiency, yet it remains challenging due to the complex interactions between excitation parameters and tree structural characteristics. In this study, a pendulum dynamics model of the fruit-branch system was established, and a multidimensional dataset was collected through field tests. Six machine learning models were subsequently trained and evaluated using this dataset. Results showed that the Random Forest (RF) model provided the best predictive performance, with mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R2) values of 1.05, 1.73, and 0.79, respectively. Subsequently, the SHAP method was employed to interpret the RF model and quantify feature importance. The analysis revealed that excitation parameters were the primary determinants of fruit inertial force, contributing 73.6%, compared with 26.4% from tree structural parameters. Among all features, excitation frequency exhibited the greatest influence, contributing 42.06%. Feature selection further improved the predictive performance of the RF model. On the test set, the MAE, RMSE, and R2 values were 1.01, 1.64, and 0.82, respectively. Field validation tests confirmed a low error rate of 6.22% between the model predictions and the measured inertial forces. These findings provide a theoretical basis for precision vibration harvesting of Camellia oleifera and offer a useful reference for the harvesting of other forest fruits.

title: Design and development of a low-cost industrial prototype of spot-specific spraying system for potato weed detection using deep learning
abstract: Conventional sprayers uniformly distribute agrochemicals on crops, even though weed distribution is typically patchy, leading to increased costs and environmental pollution. Spot-specific AI-driven sprayer offers a solution to optimize this challenge. The primary objective of this research is to develop a low-cost, smart, and fast-response industrial prototype of the spot-specific spraying system integrated with deep learning-based object detection techniques. The study aims to distinguish various weed species to enable the precise application of herbicides on potato crops. To ensure a real-world representation, a diverse dataset was collected from the real potato fields, covering various climatic conditions, irrigation methods, and timestamps. This data was utilized for training YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv12 detection models, resulting in detection accuracies of 90%, 92%, and 93% respectively. The results indicate that the YOLOv12 model obtained higher detection accuracy while localizing the weed instances accurately. Additionally, the average processing speed of 35 frames per second and 320 ms lag time between image acquisition and activation demonstrate the efficacy of the adopted YOLOv12 model. Following the result analysis, the high detection model (YOLOv12) is integrated with the spot-specific sprayer system for real-time detection of weeds in potato fields. The system accurately identified the weeds in the potato field and triggered the nozzles accordingly. The microcontroller is responsible for controlling this system to ensure the precise application of weedicide. The results indicate that the developed spot-specific sprayer system not only achieves a nearly 40% reduction in herbicide usage, leading to cost savings, but also reduces the environmental impact.

title: Comparative evaluation of machine learning models integrated with optimization algorithms for daily transpiration estimation in citrus orchards of dry-hot valley region in China
abstract: Accurate estimation of canopy transpiration (T) is essential for optimizing irrigation scheduling and improving water-use efficiency. Machine learning (ML) approaches have become critical for T estimation in smart agriculture. This study was conducted in citrus orchards within the Yuanjiang Dry-hot Valley, Yunnan Province, China. From 2020 to 2022, sap flow was monitored using thermal dissipation probes (TDP), and these data were integrated with multi-source meteorological and soil variables to develop T estimation models. The Random Forest-Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) algorithm was applied for feature selection. Twelve models were developed by combining three ML models, Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), with three hyperparameter tuning algorithms, Grid Search (GS), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the drivers of the best-performing model. Results demonstrated that RF-RFE effectively reduced input variables from 17 to 5 key factors: day of year (DOY), average air temperature (Ta), wind speed (u2), soil volumetric water content (VWC), and actual vapor pressure (ea). Among the 12 models, the GWO-XGB combination achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.91, KGE = 0.94, and RMSE = 0.18 mm d-1), ranking first in the Global Performance Indicator (GPI). SHAP analysis further revealed that DOY characterized seasonal climatic variations and phenological rhythms, Ta and u2 positively contributed to T, while ea showed a negative contribution, and VWC imposed a limiting effect at low levels. The proposed RF-RFE and GWO–XGB framework provides accurate and interpretable T estimation using only five key inputs. It offers a practical and scalable solution for precision irrigation decision support in dry-hot valleys.

title: RapeseedNet: a lightweight deep learning model for rapeseed quality detection based on near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Rapid detection of key quality indicators of rapeseed and edge deployment are crucial for improving oil processing efficiency, ensuring feed safety, and optimizing storage management. This study analyzed the responses of oil content, protein content, glucosinolate content, and moisture content of 681 rapeseed samples from multiple varieties and regions to near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR). It also explored the effects of different preprocessing methods and data partitioning strategies on model performance. To address the limitations of traditional detection methods (time-consuming, destructive) and insufficient generalization of existing models, a base model RapeseedNet-Base was constructed by fusing ResNet modules, Transformer encoder layers, and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP). This model outperformed traditional machine learning methods in quality prediction tasks, with determination coefficients (R2) of 0.893, 0.818, 0.917, and 0.815 for oil content, protein content, glucosinolate content, and moisture content prediction on the test set, respectively. Through multi-scale knowledge distillation and unstructured pruning optimization, it was upgraded to a lightweight model RapeseedNet, with a 61.2% reduction in parameters, 56% shorter computation time, and no significant loss of accuracy. After deploying the model to a portable detector, on-site verification showed R2 = 0.867 for oil content prediction and R2 = 0.819 for glucosinolate content prediction, with a single detection time of approximately 15 s, meeting real-time detection needs. This study provides strong technical support for rapid rapeseed quality detection and precise processing, and also offers a reference for non-destructive detection of other oilseed crops.

title: Agrosense v2: An AI-enabled system for precision orchard sensing and tree-level monitoring
abstract: Precision orchard management requires robust sensing systems that operate reliably under unstructured field conditions while providing actionable, tree-level information. Despite advances in computer vision and edge computing, most approaches focus on isolated tasks and lack integration into deployable, orchard-scale systems. This study presents Next-Generation Agrosense (Agrosense v2), an AI-enabled, system-oriented framework for real-time orchard sensing and tree-level monitoring. Agrosense v2 integrates tree detection and counting, canopy density classification, tree height estimation (inherited from Agrosense v1, not validated in detail in this study), and detection-based fruit counting on both the tree and the ground into a unified pipeline. Compared with the previous version (Agrosense v1), Agrosense v2 improves tree identification through temporal tracking, strengthens canopy density classification by leveraging image sequences, and adds fruit counting via image-level detection, with all outputs aggregated into tree-level spatiotemporal summaries, presented by a self-developed tree-level visualization tool. Field experiments in three citrus orchards with contrasting management conditions totaled 3,696 trees across two commercial orchards (Field A&B) and a research station (SWFREC). Tree counting accuracies were 95.96% (SWFREC), 92.73% (Field A), and 97.79% (Field B), and canopy density classification accuracies were 94.1% to 96.8%. For fruit detection, the transformer-based RT-DETR model achieved the highest mAP@0.5 up to 0.837 and 0.722 for fruits on the tree and ground, respectively, demonstrating robustness under dense canopy and cluttered ground conditions. To our knowledge, Agrosense v2 is the first real-time, field-deployable orchard sensing system that delivers multiple tree-level attributes within a single framework. By unifying perception, inference, and geo-referenced aggregation, Agrosense v2 provides a scalable foundation for data-driven precision orchard management.

title: KDYOLO-Tracker: A Deep Learning Approach to Behavior Recognition and Tracking for Sika Deer
abstract: Accurate recognition and tracking of basic behaviors are key to intelligent health monitoring for sika deer farming. To solve the problems that the current object recognition algorithms have low recognition real-time and low accuracy of identity association caused by the diversity of deer farming environments and the rapid movement speed of sika deer, this research proposes an efficient sika deer behavior recognition approach KDYOLO and a tracking approach MO-Tracking, and constructs a multi-object behavior recognition and tracking method KDYOLO-Tracker. First, a sparse training mechanism is proposed which introduces a scaling factor in the batch normalization layer to adaptively screen and remove unimportant channels, so that the computational efficiency of the model is effectively improved. Second, this paper proposes to integrate the channel pruning algorithm into the KDYOLO to further reduce model size and computation, while the pruned model is fine-tuned by adjusting the learning rate and parameters to mitigate potential accuracy losses. In addition, this paper proposes a multi-object tracking algorithm MO-Tracking, which enhances the matching space for trajectory by expanding the detection buffer, to improve the accuracy of trajectory association. The proposed KDYOLO recognition algorithm is embedded into the MO-Tracking to construct the KDYOLO-Tracker tracking model, so that the performances of recognition and tracking are further improved. The experimental results show: compared with YOLOv8l, the proposed KDYOLO not only improves the detection accuracy but also reduces the model complexity (GFLOPs, parameters, and size) by more than 58%, among which GFLOPs are reduced by 71.66%; the mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of KDYOLO reach 97.20% and 85.90%, respectively. Compared with mainstream algorithms of SSD, Faster R-CNN, and different versions of YOLO, KDYOLO consistently maintains the highest accuracy, with mAP@0.5 increased by up to 17.05% and mAP@0.5:0.95 increased by up to 31.46%. In terms of tracking performance, the HOTA, MOTA, MOTP, and IDF1 of KDYOLO-Tracker reach 85.70%, 88.30%, 93.60%, and 90.30%, respectively, which are all the highest compared with those of the five multi-object tracking algorithms DeepSort, ByteTrack, DeepMot, BotSort, and MO-Tracking. In addition, the detection speed of KDYOLO-Tracker has reached 108FPS, an increase of 19FPS compared with that without improvement. This research provides the technical support for monitoring the health status and alerting for abnormal behavior of livestock farming animals.

title: RT-BFE network: A lightweight deep learning model for real-time beef freshness evaluation and edge devices deployment
abstract: Real-time and non-destructive assessment of beef freshness is crucial for food safety, quality control, and waste reduction. However, routine evaluation still relies on destructive laboratory measurements or computationally heavy vision models that are difficult to deploy on consumer-level devices. Here, we develop a lightweight real-time beef freshness evaluation (RT-BFE) network that links image features to spoilage-related regions and is suitable for deployment on edge devices. First, total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) and total viable counts (TVC) were measured in beef samples (420 pieces stored for 0–6 days) to define three freshness levels (fresh, accepted, and deteriorated). Second, beef images in RGB, HSV, and L*a*b* color spaces were compared to find the optimal color space for beef freshness evaluation. Third, three modules, namely efficient bottleneck (E-bneck), cascade atrous spatial pyramid pooling (CASPP), and convolutional block attention module (CBAM), were designed in the RT-BFE network to strengthen its recognition ability and reduce computational cost. Finally, the model was quantized and deployed on edge devices for practical applications. Experimental results show that the L*a*b* provides the most discriminative representation for beef freshness classification. Comparative experiments against ten image classification CNNs demonstrate that the RT-BFE model achieves a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency, attaining the Accuracy and F1 of 95.238% and 95.238% with only 1.106 M Parameters and 59.347 M FLOPs, and reaching 72.301 frames per second. Subsequently, the proposed RT-BFE model is successfully deployed on edge devices in FP16-quantized form for practical applications. The deployments on a smartphone and a Jetson Orin Nano platform achieve average inference times of 32 ms and 14 ms, respectively, while maintaining an accuracy of 93.33% on both devices, demonstrating real-time inference capability and confirming its potential for in-situ beef freshness monitoring in practical agri-food scenarios.

title: Development and application of a deep learning (SF-TPP)-based intelligent detection system for granular fertilizer deposition distribution patterns
abstract: The performance evaluation of fertilizer spreaders is essential for improving the efficiency and accuracy of fertilizer application in modern agriculture. Traditional methods, such as manual collection boxes, are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for intelligent agricultural systems. To address these limitations, this study proposes a deep learning-based intelligent detection system for analyzing granular fertilizer deposition distribution patterns. The system integrates image acquisition, data processing, visualization, and storage functions, enabling real-time detection and operational optimization. A novel segmentation model, SF-TPP, was developed by combining a swin transformer backbone with a path aggregation network (PANet), region proposal network (RPN), ROI alignment, and enhanced by CBAM and feature refinement modules. Comparative experiments demonstrated that SF-TPP outperformed conventional models (F-TPP, SOLO, YOLOv5), achieving 92.8% precision, 91.3% recall, and an F1 score of 0.920. A strong correlation (R2 = 0.9626) was established between pixel area and fertilizer mass, enabling accurate mass estimation. Field experiments showed that the system achieved low mean absolute errors in key metrics, including a CV MAE of 0.99 and a fertilization amount MAE of 0.76 g. These results demonstrate the system’s high accuracy and practical potential for supporting precision agriculture.

title: Machine learning–based decision support for harvest optimization in commercial microalgae photobioreactors: A field validation study
abstract: Operational decision-making in commercial microalgae cultivation remains largely heuristic despite the increasing availability of high-frequency farm data. In photobioreactor-based production systems, harvest fraction selection is a key management decision that affects short-term biomass recovery, culture stability, and overall production efficiency. This study presents a machine learning–based decision-support framework for optimizing harvest management in commercial tubular photobioreactors cultivating Nannochloropsis sp. The framework integrates three years of heterogeneous farm data, including operational logs, meteorological variables, and FlowCam (a digital imaging system used to measure microalgae concentration and cell morphology) data. A supervised regression approach was used to predict next-day post-harvest cell concentration, and several learning algorithms were evaluated. A Random Forest model achieved the best predictive performance (R2 = 0.705), demonstrating robust prediction under noisy commercial production conditions. The trained model was implemented in an inference module that evaluates candidate harvest fractions and recommends the fraction expected to maximize short-term biomass recovery. The system was validated in a four-week farm-scale experiment across 12 commercial photobioreactors (96 planned harvest events), comparing model-guided and operator-guided harvest decisions. While the machine learning–guided strategy achieved comparable productivity levels to expert human decision-making, it reduced variability. These results provide a successful proof-of-concept for the operational feasibility of a data-driven framework to stabilize and scale commercial microalgae management. These findings demonstrate the practical feasibility of integrating machine learning into daily farm operations as a hybrid human–AI decision-support layer. The proposed framework highlights the potential of data-driven decision systems to enhance stability and scalability in commercial microalgae photobioreactor production.

title: An integrated SNR-adaptive diffusion model and lightweight dual-backbone network for orchard obstacle detection under dataset imbalance and edge deployment constraints
abstract: Accurate and real-time obstacle detection plays a critical role in ensuring the safety and operational reliability of orchard robots. However, existing detection frameworks are constrained by class imbalance prevalent in agricultural datasets, which degrades model performance, in addition to the high computational overhead associated with Transformer architectures, thereby hindering practical implementation in resource-limited edge platforms. To overcome these limitations, the present work introduces a framework that integrates a novel generative data augmentation strategy with a lightweight dual-backbone detection network. First, a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) adaptive normalization denoising diffusion probabilistic model (SNRA-DDPM) was designed to mitigate the scarcity of minority class samples. By incorporating an SNR-aware adaptive normalization mechanism, SNRA-DDPM dynamically regulates feature distributions according to noise intensity, thereby generating high-fidelity samples to effectively rebalance the dataset distribution. Second, a lightweight detector, DBFNet, was developed based on the Transformer architecture. This network employs a dual-backbone structure combining High-Performance Graphics Processing Unit Network version 2 (HGNetv2) with an improved Cross Stage Partial Darknet (CSPDarknet), designed to synergistically capture global semantic information and fine-grained frequency-domain features. Furthermore, a dual-backbone fusion (DFusion) module was designed to address the inherent feature heterogeneity between the two backbones. This module utilizes channel and position attention mechanisms to adaptively align and fuse these features, significantly enhancing cross-branch information interaction and feature complementarity. The experimental results showed that SNRA-DDPM obtained Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores of 42.8348 and 46.4346 for minority classes, including baskets and ladders, respectively, exceeding the performance of the standard DDPM. In detection tasks, DBFNet achieved an 88.21% mean Average Precision (mAP) and 208.79 frames per second (FPS) with only 34.1 giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs), surpassing the Real-Time DEtection TRansformer based on Residual Network-18 (RT-DETR-r18) baseline in both accuracy and efficiency. Notably, the integration of the SNRA-DDPM augmentation strategy further improved model accuracy. Deployment on a harvesting robot platform showed that the proposed method achieved an inference speed of 44.48 FPS at 640-pixel resolution using 16-bit floating-point (FP16) precision, corresponding to a 17.2% improvement over the baseline and confirming its real-time capability in orchards. These results demonstrate that integrating generative data augmentation with lightweight detection networks is both effective and engineering-feasible for alleviating data imbalance and enabling deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in agricultural vision tasks.

title: Active and incremental learning with RAUNet for advancing soil cover monitoring from mobile digital imaging through deep learning
abstract: Effective soil cover management is vital for sustainable agriculture, influencing soil health, erosion control, and carbon sequestration. Conventional monitoring methods are labor-intensive and often fail to capture spatial and temporal variations in soil and crop residues. To address this, we developed a deep learning framework utilizing the Residual Attention UNet (RAUNet) and a unique dataset comprising diverse residue types and agricultural scenarios. Active and incremental learning paradigms were employed to iteratively enhance segmentation accuracy by targeting underrepresented and complex scenarios, reducing the need for full model retraining. RAUNet demonstrated superior performance, achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.09%, precision of 97.08%, and an F1-Score of 96.00% for residue segmentation. Validation against traditional dot-screen methods and ground-truth data confirmed its effectiveness in segmenting bare soil, green cover, and crop residue. The model excelled in challenging agricultural conditions, including diverse textures, lighting variations, and occlusions, underscoring its robustness and adaptability. This framework enhances mapping accuracy and efficiency and supports sustainable farming by accommodating environmental and agricultural variability. RAUNet’s lightweight design facilitates its integration with drone and satellite imagery, enabling real-time, large-scale residue monitoring. By setting a new benchmark in soil cover mapping, this approach paves the way for scalable AI applications in agriculture, promoting precision and sustainability.

title: An automatic parameter search framework for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification by deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification aims to automatically distinguish field operation scenes and road driving scenes by leveraging the spatiotemporal features of massive agricultural machinery trajectories and is a key basis task in precision agriculture. In recent years, machine learning algorithms have been increasingly applied to agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification. However, these models typically depend on hyperparameters, and the empirically determined parameter structures often limit the model’s potential performance, resulting in inferior generalization across different trajectory scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose a parameter search framework based on deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning (DWIDRL) for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification, which can automatically determine the parameter structure according to the features of trajectory samples. First, we leveraged deep reinforcement learning to model parameter search as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and developed an automated parameter search framework, enabling intelligent parameter optimization. Second, it incorporates the state aggregation context module, which encodes both global and local states, enabling the model to adaptively search for parameters according to different trajectory scenarios. Third, we propose a deeply weakly informed learning strategy that enables the model to interact with the agent’s output, adaptively adjusting the optimal parameter search policy based on past experience. Finally, to increase the accuracy of the parameters within extensive search spaces, we propose a gradual search mechanism based on parameter space attenuation, which methodically narrows the search scope at each successive layer, thereby significantly improving the precision of the results. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we conducted parameter optimization experiments on five agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification models across four distinct trajectory scenarios. Consequently, on one trajectory dataset, our method achieves a maximum improvement of 20.95% in average F1-score and 15.31% in accuracy. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances model performance and generalizability by identifying optimal parameter configurations in a shorter amount of time.

title: A ConvNeXt–Liquid Neural Network framework for accurate RL disease classification
abstract: Accurate identification of Rice Leaf (RL) diseases plays a vital role in precision agriculture and global food security. This study proposes a hybrid ConvNeXt–Liquid Neural Network (ConvNeXt–LNN) framework for classification of RL diseases using image data acquired under real-field scenarios. The proposed architecture couples hierarchical convolutional feature extraction provided by ConvNeXt with the continuous-time learning dynamics of LNNs, thereby enabling refinement of disease-related feature representations for RL disease classification. The proposed framework is evaluated on a benchmark RL image dataset comprising ten categories, including multiple disease types and healthy leaves collected under heterogeneous illumination, complex background conditions, and varying levels of disease severity. The proposed architecture achieves the accuracy of 97.51% compared with traditional algorithms. The proposed ConvNeXt-LNN achieves competitive classification accuracy with only 7.8 million trainable parameters, approximately 625.79 s per training epoch, and reduced computational cost. These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for future deployment in smart agriculture ecosystems, including mobile, edge, and UAV-based crop monitoring platforms.

title: A deep learning framework for non-invasive quantification of wing and foot phenotypes in live broiler chickens
abstract: Accurate phenotypic quantification in poultry is essential for precision breeding and genetic improvement. Recent advances in deep learning have substantially improved the automation and accuracy of phenotyping. However, non-invasive and precise measurement of specific anatomical traits, particularly wings and feet, remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a CT imaging-based framework combined with deep learning to quantify wing and foot characteristics in live chickens. Specifically, we develop the DGCUNet for estimating the volumes of eight phenotypic targets associated with wings and feet. The encoder incorporates dilation transformer modules and stage-specific learning strategies to capture hierarchical representations, while the decoder employs a multi-scale fusion architecture to enhance feature integration. Four CT datasets covering multiple chicken breeds are constructed to validate the proposed framework. On the WB2024 dataset, five-fold cross-validation results demonstrate that DGCUNet achieves a Dice similarity coefficient of 86.41%, a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 3.28 mm, and an average symmetric surface distance of 0.69 mm. Furthermore, regression models establish relationships between segmented volumes and ground truth weights, and Bland-Altman analysis illustrates the agreement between estimated and actual weights. Overall, our framework enables fine-grained quantification of individual phenotypic traits rather than coarse whole-body measurements, demonstrating the potential of CT imaging and deep learning for advancing poultry phenotyping.

title: Pre-symptomatic detection of late blight in potatoes using field spectroscopy and backpropagation neural networks
abstract: Late blight (LB), caused by Phytophthora infestans, remains one of the most destructive diseases in potato (Solanum tuberosum) production. Early detection, before the emergence of visual symptoms, is critical for timely intervention and sustainable disease management. However, previous research has highlighted the challenges of consistent LB detection under variable field conditions, growth stages, and resistance levels. This study investigates the potential of machine learning models, specifically a backpropagation neural network (BPNN), for the early detection of LB across diverse conditions. Spectral data (400–1650 nm) were collected using a handheld spectrometer from two potato cultivars with differing LB resistance levels (low vs. moderate) at two distinct growth stages (establishment vs. vegetative). The BPNN model achieved high accuracy rates (>95%) from the first day post-inoculation, enabling LB prediction up to four days before visual symptom onset. When data were pooled across cultivars and growth stages, a BPNN model trained on time-series data maintained an overall accuracy of 94%, highlighting the importance of temporal data in enhancing detection robustness. Notably, the most informative wavelengths were identified in the short-wave infrared (1100–1650 nm) range. However, the use of the full spectral range proved necessary for reliable detection across varied conditions, as no single wavelength subset consistently provided optimal results. These findings support the integration of BPNN-based spectral tools for precise, pre-symptomatic LB detection, offering a promising pathway for precision agriculture to reduce fungicide application and secure potato yields.

title: YOLOv8-MST: a lightweight and efficient real-time detection and counting deep learning algorithm for double-grain peanut seeding
abstract: Double‑seed precision hill‑drop seeding is a critical technique for ensuring effective peanut emergence, where precise seeding quality relies heavily on high‑performance seed metering devices and real‑time operational monitoring. Traditional manual monitoring is inefficient for enclosed, high-speed air-suction duckbill seeders. Conventional photoelectric sensors fail to identify seed number per hill, seed damage, and impurity inclusion, while existing machine vision methods suffer from excessive computational overhead and cannot support high‑precision real‑time monitoring on low‑cost embedded devices. To address these issues, this paper proposed an edge computing-assisted deep learning monitoring method for peanut hill-drop seeding quality and developed an improved YOLOv8s-based detection and counting algorithm (YOLOv8-MST). All data collection and model training were conducted on a test bench at Qingdao University of Technology, Qingdao, China. A total of 11,130 peanut seeding images were collected and partitioned at the video session level to avoid temporal data leakage, yielding 7,769 training, 2,277 validation, and 1,084 test images following a 70%:20%:10% split. Precision, recall, AP, and mAP were adopted as the model evaluation metrics. In the network design, MobileNetV3 was applied as the lightweight backbone for seed feature extraction. The parameter-free SimAM attention mechanism was introduced to enhance feature representation of stacked and damaged seeds, and Focal_GIoU was used for bounding box regression. Furthermore, the Kalman filter combined with the Hungarian algorithm was embedded to optimize object tracking and improve counting accuracy. Experimental results showed that the proposed YOLOv8‑MST achieved a competitive performance with a compact size of 3.88 M parameters, a mAP of 92.9%, and an average inference speed of 15.7 FPS. Compared with the original YOLOv8s, the frame rate was improved by 54.05%. The proposed algorithm accurately identified seeding status and counted qualified holes, achieving promising accuracy and real-time capability in complex scenarios, which satisfied the on-site real-time monitoring requirements of peanut double-seed hill-drop seeding.

title: A lightweight dual-task transformer framework with geometry-constrained path extraction for autonomous under-canopy navigation in maize fields
abstract: To address the challenges of reliable perception and navigation in under-canopy maize environments, this study proposes a lightweight dual-task perception-to-navigation framework that jointly performs road and obstacle segmentation and generates geometry-constrained navigation lines. Experiments on a self-collected dataset containing 5051 annotated images show that UC-TwinLiteFormer achieves 95.3 % road mIoU and 86.7 % obstacle mIoU with only 1.46 M parameters, demonstrating a favourable balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Building upon the segmentation results, the proposed GCP-NLE converts semantic predictions into structured navigation paths under obstacle-free, non-bypassable, and bypassable scenarios. Jetson Nano deployment and closed-loop navigation simulation further demonstrate the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the complete perception-to-navigation pipeline. Overall, the proposed framework provides an efficient and interpretable solution for autonomous under-canopy navigation of agricultural robots. Future work will further validate the system through full-scale field robot experiments and investigate cross-region generalisation under more diverse agricultural environments. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ayi192/UC-TwinLiteFormer.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted design and optimization of Fin Ray Effect flexible grippers for lychee harvesting
abstract: The harvesting end effector plays a crucial role in agricultural robots. However, the initial design and configuration optimization have traditionally lacked intelligent methods. To address this issue, this study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI) enhanced design and optimization method to develop a novel Gripping-and-Shearing Separation Type Lychee Harvesting End Effector (GS-STLHEE). A case study designs a flexible gripper and uses numerical models to build training and testing datasets for configuration design and optimization. The nonlinear relationships between these parameters and characteristics are predicted by surrogate models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Back-propagation Artificial Neural Networks (BPANN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The Bayesian Optimization (BO) technique is then employed to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the AI-learning models. The aforementioned data-driven optimization functions and constraints are integrated with the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. Configuration parameters such as supporting beam thickness, incline angle, and spacing distance are optimized, and reaction force and gripper mass are enhanced. The results indicate the CNN model demonstrates superior learning ability, with the advancement of higher prediction accuracy, when handling complicated datasets. The optimization flexible gripper demonstrates larger reaction force and lighter mass, with an improvement rate of around 50 %.
